children: Softer crude palm oil prices are unlikely to be sustainable, given tightening supplies in Indonesia and east Malaysia amid severe El Nino conditions, Public Investment Bank analyst Chong Hoe Leong says in a note. However, the market is awaiting signs of an inventory drawdown in Malaysia before prices can recover, he says. The wide price gap between CPO and soybean oil could also encourage buyers to switch to palm oil, boosting demand and helping reduce inventories, he reckons. Public IB maintains an overweight rating on the Malaysian plantations sector, pegging Sarawak Plantation and TA Ann as top picks given their high dividend yield and production growth outpacing the industry average.(yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
